# Long ordinary computed-leaf first history

This is an informed maintenance study, not a blind authoring benchmark. The
original GPT-6/Codex context knew the sealed-T length regression and the ordinary
derived-T normalization design. One data Bit and one temporary computed ancilla
bound the desired programs; no maximum-width quantum case was generated.

The single inert packet preserves the complete original directory: **24 unchanged
files / 266,614 expanded bytes**, including three sources and edition manifests,
three before-run source notes, three saved observer drivers, three pre-call
metadata records, three final records and all six complete stdout/stderr streams.
Every original regular-file mode is `0644`, retained in the manifest and archive.
No file is filtered out, reconstructed or replaced by a later result.

| `attempt-01/main.qli`: 1,025 expanded ordinary `std::gate::t` calls | `817f6a9ea87d5a642d3861321710458fed6bca1bb4fba75e52ca3dd0f109bf23` | Source-work `limit`: 999,695 used, 925 requested while checking `std::gate::t`; the unchanged project bound is 1,000,000. |
| `attempt-02/main.qli`: separate 257-call expanded translation | `dbb73d713dc1968957916ec09e5f19ce4ce21c544c0a8dd497ea0b64cc64e155` | Source-work `limit`: 1,000,000 used, 1 requested while checking `std::gate::scalar_eighth`. |
| `attempt-03/main.qli`: separate compact static fold of 257 T calls | `b7f23d2df7fc37eb2e74c7cc1d52d97541d42f67b427c866aa345d35d3176810` | Distinct `limit`: `with_computed phase normalization: function evidence exceeds its finite IR profile`. |

All three commands exited 1, produced one JSON error diagnostic and no result,
and had empty stderr. The first prediction allowed either source-work exhaustion
or a FunctionEvidence refusal. The second and third source notes explain their
changed forms before their separate invocations. Their intended exponent modulo
eight is 1, but none of these observations establishes a successful exact
normalization. The expanded-source work limits remain unrepaired. Future repairs
and replays must use separate records; they never overwrite these first sources,
predictions, drivers or observations. No recorded source or command is executed
by the retention reader.

Each saved driver checks source hashes before the invocation, writes its own
hash and pre-call metadata, then retains complete streams and final observations.
The before/after selected input window has 206 hashes: Cargo metadata, `build.rs`,
Rust sources and bundled `.qli` sources. Those maps agree within and across all
three checks. CLI, kernel and original-source hashes also remain stable.
HEAD `460f72e019885bd859686b6f4a8b265b40ab36fd` and the dirty status were
sampled before each call and copied into its final record; they were not
independently resampled afterward. The observed CLI is
`b5b71be9a3f4ae0f134392f751390fb6fd88ed9b3329748a0b13fb9f3082e85e`,
and the explicit native kernel is
`54c9d60b80f67217abd95c8fe6ec1c06aa262e142d5e6db30f46a20cb90faf07`.

The separate routine CLI build records are under
`/private/tmp/qleisli-generic-plan-validation-ji3399kg/runtime-batch-long-baseline-cli-build.*`.
They are contextual records, not an input to this passive reader; their routine
inventories are not copied here. The actual first-call windows remain preserved
losslessly in this packet. Observed dirty inputs and executable hashes are not a
reconstructed clean commit-to-binary build attestation. These three refusals are
neither a source-success benchmark nor a source-preservation proof, M2 acceptance
authority, constitutional discharge or completion of #369/#167.

The archive uses sorted regular USTAR members, fixed metadata and deterministic
gzip. The strict passive reader checks all member hashes, modes, counts, source
lineage, observer/window associations and diagnostic distinctions under the
unchanged 80-member, 5 MiB expanded and 2 MiB stored caps. It never extracts
members and never executes archived observers, commands or source.
